Dr Kwabena Essibu, who hails from Senya Breku in the constituency, was recently elected Central Regional chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP). items.title: All 24 NDC constituency executive positions in Juaboso go unopposed
items.summary: All 24 constituency executive positions of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Juaboso have gone unopposed, with no contest required for any of the positions. The Member of Parliament for Juaboso, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, announced the outcome in a Facebook post on Saturday, October 24, congratulating the executives on their uncontested selection.

items.title: Gadi Eisenkot campaigns on Moroccan roots in challenge to Netanyahu
items.summary: As Israel prepares to vote, Gadi Eisenkot is leveraging his Moroccan heritage in Likud strongholds such as Sderot. From historical divides to October 7, identity and trauma are redefining the city's political loyalties.

items.title: Prague honours Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
items.summary: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

items.title: Saudi Arabia looks to US for an AI edge as Yemen's Houthis up pressure
items.summary: The US is helping Saudi Arabia fight the Houthi group in Yemen with AI-assisted targeting. But AI is not a magic bullet, experts say, and there are technological, political and human rights issues to consider.

items.title: Bulgaria holds presidential elections amid divisions over Ukraine war
items.summary: Bulgarians are voting in presidential elections amid security concerns over attacks on ships in the Black Sea. The vote for the largely ceremonial post is seen as a test of the popularity of Prime Minister Rumen Radev.

items.title: At least 1,300 people arrested in mass weekend protests across France
items.summary: At least 1,300 people were arrested on the sidelines of Saturday's protests across France and at least 50 officers and three protesters were hurt, the interior ministry said Sunday. The arrests occurred as clashes broke out on the margins of largely calm demonstrations in major cities over the high cost of living.

items.title: Suspect in racist gun attack near Paris transferred to psychiatric unit
items.summary: A shooter suspected of killing one person and wounding five others on Friday in the town of Trappes, near Paris, has had his police custody suspended for a 48-hour psychiatric observation, anti-terror prosecutors said Sunday. The 39-year-old man is believed to have had racist motivations behind the gun attack as most of the victims had foreign origins.

items.title: France: Some clashes erupted at end of protests
items.summary: There were some clashes on Saturday, mainly in major cities and as demonstrations came to an end. French authorities say police made nearly 1,000 arrests nationwide. Here’s a report from our sister channel, France 2.

items.title: More than 400.000 protest across France
items.summary: Saturday’s demonstrations across France were largely peaceful, easing fears of a repeat of the violence seen last weekend. Hundreds of thousands took to the streets to demand action on the rising cost of living and more funding for public services, with students, workers and retirees marching side by side. Many say their anger shows no sign of fading. The government put turnout at 410,000 nationwide, while the CGT union estimated the figure was almost twice as high. Here’s Jack Pownall with more

items.title: France’s far right gathers as Le Pen prepares her presidential campaign
items.summary: Meanwhile, France’s far-right National Rally is holding the second day of its party congress in Orléans, south of Paris. Marine Le Pen is expected to officially launch her presidential campaign in a speech later this afternoon, while Jordan Bardella is being re-elected as party leader. On Saturday, a large counter-demonstration against the far right was held in the city. For more on what’s happening there, let’s cross to our reporter, Antonia Kerrigan.

items.title: Hundreds of thousands march in France to protest against government
items.summary: Hundreds of thousands marched across France on Saturday protesting the rising cost of living and a lack of government resources for essential services like schools. While demonstrations in Paris started peacefully they ended with a heavy security response, with almost 1,000 arrested across the country. France 24 International Affairs Editor Oliver Farry shares further details.

items.title: Serbia holds parliamentary election as populist leader Vucic faces student movement
items.summary: Serbia votes on Sunday in what is set to be its most contested parliamentary election in more than 14 years, as a student-led movement seeks to oust the party of populist leader Aleksandar Vucic. The vote comes after nearly two years of student-led protests sparked by the 2024 collapse of a canopy that killed 16 people.

items.title: What to know as Brazilians choose between Lula and Bolsonaro in tense presidential runoff
items.summary: Brazilians are set on Sunday to choose between leftist incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro in the runoff vote of a deeply polarizing presidential election, and one which will determine whether the US significantly expands its growing influence in Latin America.

items.title: Red Cross trains staff as Kenya records its second death from Ebola
items.summary: It says the fight to contain the virus does not end when a patient dies, saying the handling and burial of the body is just as important.
